spec.description: The trade tape for one product, newest first. Walked backwards in time by the id of the last row of the previous page.

request.title: GetTradesRequest
request.description: Which product, and where to resume.

product_id.description: Product id, such as `BTC-USD`. `products.list_products` returns it as `id`.

after.description: Return trades older than this `trade_id`. Confusingly named: `after` means later in the walk, which is earlier in time, because the tape is served newest first. Omit for the newest page.

before.description: Return trades newer than this `trade_id`. The other direction, for catching up rather than backfilling.

limit.description: Trades per page. Range [1, 1000]; defaults to 1000.

response.title: Trades
response.description: One page of the tape, newest first. A bare array, so the payload is itself the collection the walk ends on.

notes: The first recorded, tested use of `seek` pagination in this registry. The cursor is a genuine per-row id -- `trade_id` is unique and monotonic per product -- so no `overlap` is declared and the plain shape applies: the next request carries the `trade_id` of the last row of this one, and the walk ends on an empty page.
`done.rows` is omitted because the payload is itself the collection: the response is a bare array, not an object wrapping one.

Verified against the live API before it was declared, rather than read off the documentation: a page of three ending at `1090665550` is followed, with `after=1090665550`, by `[1090665549, 1090665548, 1090665547]`.
